name: scroll-text-marquee
title: Scroll Text Marquee
description: A full-width ticker of two oversized text lines moving sideways in opposite directions, the top white and the bottom grey. An option ties their speed to page scrolling.
use: A portfolio or landing page wants a bold moving typographic band without images or cards.
avoid: The motion never stops and the text is always cropped, so a short exact message can never be read in full.
a11y: Nothing is interactive, but the loop never pauses and each line is repeated four times, so screen readers hear the phrase over and over. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two full-bleed lines of very large, tightly tracked sans-serif text, the upper white and the lower grey, packed edge to edge so words slice off at both sides. Both lines sit on black with nothing else around them.
behaves: Each line slides continuously, the top one way and the bottom the other, with copies repeating so there is never a gap. If the scroll-linked option is on, page scrolling speeds the motion up or flips its direction.
customise: Pass the text as children and set base velocity; a misspelled clasname prop applies the type styles, and scrollDependent plus delay tune the motion.
weight: light: A few duplicated text spans driven by a frame loop; no heavy rendering.
demo: Lines read "Velocity-driven marquee" and "Scroll to change speed".
issues: Each line is repeated four times in the DOM, so screen readers and text selection hit duplicates.
The demo copy says scroll changes the speed, but scrollDependent is left off, so scrolling does nothing.
polishWhy: Bold, clean type and a smooth loop, but it is a single-purpose text ticker.
